Marissa / Laura —

Thanks for flagging. Below is a concise approach we recommend to keep this deal moving while protecting product IP:

1) Outputs: agree that Customer owns outputs. Proposed clause: "Customer Output Ownership: Customer shall retain all right, title and interest in and to (a) Customer Data and (b) Outputs generated solely from Customer Data. Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use such Outputs."

2) Training / Model Updates: do not agree to blanket prohibition on training. Counter-proposal: "No Training Without Consent: Redwood will not use Customer Data or Outputs to train or improve models used by other customers without Customer's prior written consent. Customer may opt-in to a separate Training Agreement that includes compensation, data handling measures, and deletion rights. For model improvements that are product-facing but not traceable to Customer Data (aggregated and anonymized telemetry), Redwood may continue to improve the Service."

3) Feedback license: narrow, limited-purpose. Proposed language: "Feedback License: To the extent Customer or its users provide feedback relating to the Service, Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual license to use such feedback solely to operate, maintain, and improve the Service provided to Customer, provided that such use will not incorporate Customer Data or Outputs into Redwood's foundational training datasets used to train general-purpose models without Customer's explicit written consent."

4) Acceptable mitigation/levers: isolated model instances (dedicated inference) or contractual audit rights, commercial premium for training opt-in, stronger anonymization commitments, and contractual deletion windows.

If Marissa wants, I can draft redline language for the MSA and a short proposed paragraph for the Order Form reflecting the opt-in mechanics.

Rishi
